subject: Materials Science
title: Ceramic Armor: Stopping Bullets
description: One-minute skill: Ceramic Armor: Stopping Bullets.

hook.text: A bullet hits a ceramic plate at 900 m/s. The ceramic shatters — and saves the soldier's life.

buildup.text: Boron carbide and silicon carbide are the ceramics of choice — extremely hard and lightweight.

discovery.text: The ceramic's hardness blunts and fragments the bullet on impact, spreading the energy.

twist.text: A backing layer — usually aramid fiber — catches the fragments the shattered ceramic can't stop.

climax.text: Ceramic body armor weighs half as much as equivalent steel plate — mobility saves lives too.

punchline.text: Ceramic armor works by destroying itself to destroy the bullet.

quiz.question: How does ceramic armor stop a bullet?
options: It bounces the bullet back like a spring
Its hardness blunts and fragments the bullet on impact
It melts the bullet with heat
